Fortunately Qiuwen was still with them, and she and Zijuan supported Daiyu into her room. After Qiuwen had gone, Zijuan and Xueyan stayed beside Daiyu. When they saw her gradually regain consciousness, she asked Zijuan, “Why are you two standing here crying?” Hearing her speak coherently, Zijuan felt somewhat relieved and replied, “You had just returned from Grandmother's and seemed unwell. Daiyu had learned that day of the affair between Baoyu and Baochai. It touched the secret anguish she had borne for years, and in her sudden distress and anger she had lost possession of herself. Yet after returning and coughing up that mouthful of blood, her mind gradually cleared, though she could not remember a single thing that had happened before. Now, seeing Zijuan weep, she dimly recalled what Silly Elder Sister had said. Far from grieving, she wanted only to die quickly and thereby discharge the debt she owed. Zijuan and Xueyan could only remain with her. They wanted to report the matter, but feared that, as on the previous occasion, Xifeng would accuse them of raising a needless alarm.

p.src: But when Qiuwen returned, she looked thoroughly flustered. Grandmother Jia had just awakened from her afternoon nap. Seeing Qiuwen in such a state, she asked what had happened. Terrified, Qiuwen hastily recounted everything that had just occurred. Grandmother Jia was appalled. “This is dreadful!” she exclaimed. She immediately sent for Lady Wang and Xifeng and told the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law what had happened. “I warned everyone,” said Xifeng. “Who could have let the secret slip? Does this not make matters more difficult still?” “Never mind that for now,” said Grandmother Jia. “Let us first go and see how she is.” As she spoke, she rose and went with Lady Wang, Xifeng, and the others to see Daiyu. They found Daiyu's face as white as snow, without the least trace of color; her consciousness was clouded and her breathing faint. After a long while, she suffered another fit of coughing. A maid handed her a spittoon, and all she brought up was phlegm streaked with blood. Everyone was thrown into alarm. Daiyu opened her eyes slightly. Seeing Grandmother Jia beside her, she gasped, “Grandmother, all the love you gave me has been wasted!” These words caused Grandmother Jia great pain. “My dear child,” she said, “just rest and recover. There is nothing to fear.” Daiyu smiled faintly and closed her eyes again. A maid entered from outside and reported to Xifeng, “The doctor has arrived.” Everyone accordingly withdrew a little. Doctor Wang entered with Jia Lian, felt Daiyu's pulse, and said, “There is no immediate danger. Pent-up emotion has injured her liver, and because the liver is failing to contain the blood, her mind and vitality are unsettled. She must now take medicine to conserve the yin and stop the bleeding; only then can we hope for her recovery.” Having said this, Doctor Wang went out with Jia Lian to write the prescription and have the medicine prepared.

p.src: Seeing how poorly Daiyu looked, Grandmother Jia went outside and said to Xifeng and the others, “I am not cursing the child, but I fear her illness will be difficult to cure. You should make some preparations for her as well, if only to ward off ill fortune. If she recovers, will that not be a relief to us all? And if the worst should happen, at least we shall not be thrown into confusion at the last moment. Our household already has important business in these next few days.” Xifeng agreed. Grandmother Jia questioned Zijuan once more, but still could not discover who had told Daiyu. Still perplexed, Grandmother Jia said, “It was only natural that the children, having played together from childhood, should be very fond of one another. But now that they are grown and understand the ways of the world, they ought to observe some distance. Only if a girl knows her proper conduct can I love and cherish her. If she harbors any other notion in her heart, what sort of person would that make her? Then all the love I gave her was wasted. Now that you have told me this, I am rather uneasy.” On returning to her room, she sent for Xiren and questioned her. Xiren repeated what she had told Lady Wang the other day and described Daiyu's recent condition. Grandmother Jia said, “When I saw her just now, she did not seem delirious. That is what I cannot understand. In a family such as ours, there can naturally be no improper affair; nor can such lovesickness possibly be tolerated. If this is not what ails Miss Lin, I would willingly spend any amount of money on her treatment. But if this is indeed her illness, not only can it not be cured, I shall no longer have the heart to care.” Xifeng said, “You need not worry about Cousin Lin, Grandmother. Her second cousin is seeing the doctor with her every day, in any case. The business at Aunt Xue's is more urgent. I heard early this morning that the house is nearly ready. Grandmother and Mother should go to Aunt Xue's, and I shall accompany you so that we can discuss the matter. There is only one difficulty: with Cousin Bao at Aunt Xue's, it will be awkward to speak freely. It would be better simply to invite Aunt Xue here in the evening. We could settle everything in one night, and then the arrangements would be easy.” Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang both said, “You are right. It is late today. Tomorrow after the meal, we women shall go over together.” After saying this, Grandmother Jia ate her evening meal. Xifeng and Lady Wang then returned to their respective rooms. We shall say no more of them for now.

p.src: The next day, after breakfast, Xifeng came over to test Baoyu. Entering the inner room, she said, “Congratulations, Brother Bao! Your father has chosen an auspicious day for your wedding. Are you pleased?” Hearing this, Baoyu merely gazed at Xifeng with a smile and nodded slightly. Xifeng smiled. “Would you like us to bring Cousin Lin here as your bride?” Baoyu burst into loud laughter. Watching him, Xifeng could not tell whether he understood or was still muddled, so she asked again, “Your father says he will let you marry Cousin Lin only after you recover. If you remain this foolish, he will not let you marry her.” Baoyu suddenly became solemn. “I am not foolish. You are the foolish one.” With that, he rose and said, “I shall go and see Cousin Lin and set her mind at ease.” Xifeng hastily took hold of him. “Cousin Lin already knows. Now that she is to be a bride, she is naturally shy and will not see you.” Baoyu asked, “Once she has married me and come here, will she see me or not?” Xifeng was both amused and anxious. She thought, “Xiren was right. When Cousin Lin is mentioned, though he still talks wildly, he does seem somewhat more lucid. But if he truly regains his senses and discovers afterward that the bride is not Cousin Lin, once this riddle is exposed, the resulting trouble will be almost impossible to settle.” Suppressing a smile, she said, “If you behave properly, she will see you; if you act crazily, she will not.” Baoyu said, “I have only one heart, and the other day I gave it to Cousin Lin. When she comes here, she will bring it back to me in any case and put it inside my belly again.” Hearing that this was truly mad talk, Xifeng went out and smiled at Grandmother Jia. Grandmother Jia had heard it all and felt both amused and distressed. “I heard everything long ago. For now, pay him no attention. Have Xiren comfort him properly. Let us go.”

They came forward and identified each item in turn for Grandmother Jia: “Here are gold neck rings, and here are ornaments of gold and pearls—eighty pieces altogether. Here are forty lengths of figured ceremonial brocade. Here are one hundred and twenty lengths of assorted silks and satins. Here are one hundred and twenty garments for the four seasons. No sheep or wine have been prepared outside, so here is silver in lieu of them.” Grandmother Jia approved everything, then said quietly to Xifeng, “Go and tell your aunt that these are not mere empty formalities. Ask her to wait until Pan is released and then have things made for his sister at her leisure. We shall provide the bedding for the wedding day ourselves.” Xifeng agreed. p.src: Daiyu could hardly remain seated. Her lower body ached where it pressed against the bed, but she braced herself with all her strength and called Xueyan over. “My poetry notebook,” she said. She gasped again as she spoke. Xueyan supposed she wanted the poetry manuscripts she had sorted a few days earlier, so she found them and brought them to Daiyu. Daiyu nodded, then raised her eyes toward the chest. Xueyan did not understand and merely stared blankly. Daiyu glared in vexation, then began coughing again and spat up another mouthful of blood. Xueyan hastily turned to fetch water. Daiyu rinsed her mouth and spat into a box. Zijuan wiped her mouth with a silk handkerchief. Taking the handkerchief, Daiyu pointed toward the chest. Then she was seized by such breathlessness that she could not speak and closed her eyes. “Lie back and rest a little, miss,” said Zijuan. Daiyu shook her head again. Zijuan guessed that she wanted a handkerchief, so she told Xueyan to open the chest and take out a piece of white silk. Daiyu looked at it, tossed it aside, and forced out the words, “The one with writing on it.” Only then did Zijuan understand that she wanted the old handkerchief inscribed with verses. She had no choice but to tell Xueyan to take it out and hand it to Daiyu. Zijuan urged her, “Rest a while, miss. Why tire yourself again? Wait until you are better before looking at it.” But once Daiyu had it in her hand, she did not even look at the verses. Struggling, she stretched out one hand and tried with all her might to tear the silk, but her hand could do nothing but tremble, and she had no strength to rend it. Zijuan already knew that she resented Baoyu, but dared not say so openly. She only said, “Why make yourself angry again, miss?” Daiyu nodded, tucked it into her sleeve, and told Xueyan to light a lamp. Xueyan assented and quickly lit the lamp.

p.src: Daiyu looked at them, then sat with her eyes closed again. After panting for a while, she said, “Put a cover over the brazier.” Zijuan supposed that she was cold. So she said, “Miss, lie down and put another quilt over yourself. I fear you cannot bear the charcoal fumes.” Daiyu shook her head again. Xueyan had no choice but to cover the brazier and set it on its stand on the floor. Daiyu nodded, meaning that it should be moved onto the kang. Xueyan had to carry it up, then went out to fetch the low brazier table used on the kang. Daiyu raised herself, and Zijuan had to support her with both hands. Only then did Daiyu take the silk handkerchief from before in her hand. Gazing at the fire, she nodded and tossed it onto the flames. Zijuan started in fright and wanted to snatch it away, but dared not move either hand. Xueyan had gone out again to fetch the brazier table, and by then the handkerchief had already caught fire. Zijuan pleaded, “Miss, why are you doing this?” Daiyu pretended not to hear. Reaching back, she picked up her poetry manuscripts, looked at them, and set them down again. Fearing that she meant to burn those too, Zijuan hurriedly leaned against Daiyu and freed one hand to take them, but Daiyu had already picked them up and thrown them onto the fire. Zijuan could not reach them and could only fret helplessly. Just then Xueyan came in carrying the table. Seeing Daiyu toss something down, she did not know what it was, but hurried to seize it. The instant the paper touched the fire it ignited; how could it wait for her? It was already blazing fiercely. Heedless of burning her hands, Xueyan snatched the papers from the fire, threw them onto the floor, and stamped wildly on them, but little remained unburned. Daiyu closed her eyes and fell backward, almost bearing Zijuan to the floor beneath her. Zijuan quickly called Xueyan over, and together they supported Daiyu and laid her down, while Zijuan’s heart thumped wildly. She thought of calling someone, but it was already late; yet if she called no one, she feared that she, Xueyan, Yingge, and the other young maids might be unable to cope if anything suddenly happened. With great difficulty, they endured the night. Early the next morning, Daiyu seemed to have rallied a little. After the meal, however, she suddenly began coughing and vomiting again, and her condition grew grave once more. Seeing an ominous turn, Zijuan hurriedly called Xueyan and the others in to keep watch while she went to report to Grandmother Jia. But when she reached Grandmother Jia’s apartments, all was silent. Only two or three old serving women and several maids who did rough work were there minding the rooms. Zijuan asked, “Where is the Old Lady?” They all said they did not know. Surprised by this answer, Zijuan went to Baoyu’s rooms to look, but no one was there either. She questioned the maids of the household, but they too said they did not know. Zijuan now understood most of what had happened. “But how can these people be so heartless and cold!”

p.src: Then she reflected that not a single person had come to ask after Daiyu these past few days. The more she thought about it, the more grieved she became, until a surge of pent-up anger seized her and she wheeled around and left. She thought to herself, “Today I shall see what Baoyu looks like! Let me see how he can face me! That year, one lie from me made him fall desperately ill, yet today he has openly done such a thing! Truly, the hearts of all men beneath heaven are colder than ice and snow—enough to make one gnash one’s teeth!” Thinking as she walked, she soon arrived at Happy Red Court. She saw that the courtyard gate stood ajar, but inside it was utterly still. It suddenly occurred to Zijuan, “Since he is getting married, naturally there must be a new bridal chamber. But where can it be?” As she lingered there, looking this way and that, she saw Moyu running past and called him to stop. Moyu came over grinning and asked, “What are you doing here, Sister?” Zijuan said, “I heard that Second Master Bao was getting married, so I came to see the excitement. But it turns out it is not being held here, and I do not even know what day it is to be.” Moyu said quietly, “I’ll tell only you, Sister, but you must not tell Xueyan and the others. Of course it will not be here—the Master ordered Second Master Lian to prepare other rooms.” Then he asked, “Did you want something, Sister?” “Nothing,” Zijuan replied. “Run along.” Moyu ran off again. Zijuan stood there dazed for a while. Suddenly remembering Daiyu, she realized that even now she did not know whether her mistress was alive or dead. Her eyes brimming with tears, she clenched her teeth and said fiercely, “Baoyu, if she dies tomorrow, you may think you have succeeded in hiding away and not seeing her! Before she had reached Bamboo Lodge, she saw two young maids peering out from inside the gate. The moment one of them spotted her, she cried, “Isn’t that Sister Zijuan coming?” Zijuan knew something was wrong. She quickly waved for them not to shout and hurried inside. At one glance, Nanny Wang burst into loud sobs. Zijuan had thought that Nanny Wang, being advanced in years, might lend her courage. Who could have known that the woman would be utterly at a loss, leaving Zijuan more anxious and unsettled than ever? Suddenly someone occurred to her, and she ordered a young maid to hurry and fetch that person.

p.src: A young maid at the entrance to the inner room had already seen her and announced, “The First Mistress is here.” Zijuan hurried out and came face-to-face with Li Wan. Li Wan anxiously asked, “How is she?” Zijuan tried to speak, but her throat was choked with sobs and she could not utter a single word. Her tears fell like pearls from a broken string, and she merely reached one hand behind her and pointed toward Daiyu. The sight of Zijuan in such a state made Li Wan's heart ache all the more. She asked no further questions and hurried over. When she looked, Daiyu was already unable to speak. Li Wan softly called to her twice. Daiyu opened her eyes a little, as though she were still conscious, but only her eyelids and lips showed the faintest movement. Breath still passed in and out of her mouth, yet she could neither speak a word nor shed a single tear. Li Wan turned and, seeing that Zijuan was no longer beside her, asked Xueyan where she was. “She is in the outer room,” Xueyan replied. Li Wan hurried out and found Zijuan lying on an empty bed in the outer room, her face a sickly blue-yellow. Her eyes were closed, but tears continued to stream from them, and her tears and mucus had soaked a bowl-sized patch of the flower-patterned, brocade-edged mattress. Li Wan quickly called to her, and only then did Zijuan slowly open her eyes and raise herself up. Li Wan said, “Silly girl, this is no time to think only of your own grief! Why have you not brought out Miss Lin's clothes and bedding and changed her into them? What are you waiting for? She is a young lady—surely you do not mean to let her come naked into this world and depart from it naked too!” At these words, Zijuan could restrain herself no longer and burst into bitter sobs. Li Wan wept and fretted at once. Wiping away her tears, she patted Zijuan on the shoulder and said, “Good child, your crying has thrown my heart into utter confusion. Hurry and put her things in order. If we delay any longer, it will be too late.” Amid this commotion, someone came rushing in from outside in a panic, giving Li Wan a fright. She looked and saw that it was Ping'er. When Ping'er ran in and saw the scene, she merely stood there staring in stunned silence. Li Wan asked, “Why have you come here at a time like this instead of staying over there?” As she spoke, Mrs. Lin Zhixiao also came in. Ping'er replied, “Mistress was worried and sent me to see how things were. Since you are here, First Mistress, our mistress can devote herself entirely to matters on the other side.” Li Wan nodded. Ping'er said, “I should like to see Miss Lin too.” As she spoke, she went into the inner room, tears already streaming down her face. Meanwhile, Li Wan said to Mrs. Lin Zhixiao, “You have come at just the right time. Hurry out and see to things. Tell the stewards to prepare for Miss Lin's funeral. When everything is properly arranged, have one of them report back to me; there is no need to go to the other side.” Mrs. Lin Zhixiao assented, but remained standing there.

p.src: Now, when Xueyan saw all these preparations, she thought of her own young mistress and could not help feeling heartsick; but in the presence of Grandmother Jia and Xifeng she dared not show it. She thought to herself, “I do not know what they want me for. I had better watch and see. Baoyu used to be inseparable from our young mistress, as close as honey blended with oil, yet now he never sees her. Who knows whether his illness is real or feigned? Perhaps, fearing that our young mistress would not consent, he pretended to have lost his jade and acted the fool so that she would lose heart. His intention must be to marry Miss Bao. I will go and look at him and see whether he still acts foolish when he sees me. Surely he cannot still be pretending today!” Thinking thus, she slipped to the doorway of the inner room and peeped inside. Though he still uttered a few foolish remarks, his condition was altogether different from what it had been during his illness. At the sight, Xueyan felt both angry and heartbroken. What are you wearing this wretched thing for?” He was about to pull it off, making Grandmother Jia break out in a cold sweat from alarm. Then Baoyu reconsidered: “Cousin Lin is easily offended. I must not act rashly.” After waiting a little longer, however, he still could not restrain himself and went forward to lift it. The bridal attendant took the veil from him, Xueyan withdrew, and Yinger and the others came forward to wait upon the bride. Baoyu opened his eyes and looked. The bride seemed to be Baochai, but he could not believe it. Holding a lamp in one hand, he rubbed his eyes with the other and looked again—and was it not Baochai after all! There she sat in splendid cosmetics and gorgeous robes, her shoulders full and her body supple, her coiffure low and her side-locks drooping, her eyes lowered with a faint, fleeting glance: truly like a lotus dusted with powder and hung with dew, or apricot blossoms softened by mist. Baoyu stood dazed for a while. Then he noticed Yinger standing beside him, while Xueyan had disappeared. Baoyu no longer knew what to think and decided that he must be dreaming. He merely stood there in a stupor. The others took the lamp from him and helped him sit down again. His eyes stared straight ahead, and he did not utter a word. Afraid that his illness was returning, Grandmother Jia personally helped him onto the bed. Xifeng and Madam You invited Baochai into the inner room and seated her on the bed. Baochai naturally kept her head lowered and said nothing. After Baoyu had collected himself somewhat, he saw Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang sitting nearby and softly called to Xiren, “Where am I? Is this not a dream?” Xiren said, “This is your happy day. Do not talk such nonsense about dreams. Your father is outside, you know.” Baoyu pointed quietly and asked, “Who is that beauty sitting over there?” Xiren covered her mouth, laughing too hard to speak. Only after a long while did she manage to say, “She is the new Second Young Mistress.” Everyone else turned their heads away, unable to suppress their laughter. Baoyu said again, “How muddle-headed! Tell me, who exactly is this Second Young Mistress?” Xiren replied, “Miss Bao.” “What about Miss Lin?” asked Baoyu. Xiren said, “Your father arranged for you to marry Miss Bao. Why are you talking such nonsense about Miss Lin?” Baoyu said, “But I saw Miss Lin just now, and Xueyan was there too. How can you say she is not here? What kind of trick are you all playing on me?” Xifeng came over and said softly, “Miss Bao is sitting inside the room. Do not talk nonsense. If you offend her later, the Old Lady will not stand for it.” On hearing this, Baoyu grew even more confused. He already suffered from spells of delirium, and the uncanny events of that night left him more bewildered than ever. Disregarding everything else, he kept insisting that he must go and find Cousin Lin.

p.src: Early the next morning, Jia Zheng took leave of the ancestral shrine and went to bid Grandmother Jia farewell, saying respectfully, “Your unfilial son must travel far from you. I ask only that you take good care of yourself as the seasons change. As soon as I reach my post, I shall write to pay my respects and inquire after your health, so please do not worry about me. Baoyu’s marriage has now been concluded in accordance with your wishes. I ask only that you continue to instruct him.” Grandmother Jia feared that Jia Zheng would worry while on the road, so she said nothing of Baoyu’s relapse. She merely told him, “There is one thing I must tell you. Although Baoyu was married last night, the marriage was not consummated. Since you are leaving today, he ought by rights to accompany you some distance on your way. The wedding was held to dispel his illness, and he has only just begun to recover. After all yesterday’s exertions, I fear that going outdoors might expose him to a chill. That is why I ask you: if you wish him to see you off, I shall send for him at once; but if you mean to spare him, I shall have someone bring him here so that you may see him, and let him simply kowtow to you.” Jia Zheng replied, “What need is there for him to see me off? If only he will apply himself seriously to his studies from now on, that would please me far more than any farewell.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia felt another weight lift from her mind. She asked Jia Zheng to sit down, then sent Yuanyang away with detailed instructions to bring Baoyu, accompanied by Xiren. Yuanyang had not been gone long when Baoyu duly arrived, and he was again told to perform the proper obeisance. At the sight of his father, Baoyu collected himself somewhat. For a little while his mind was clear, and nothing seemed seriously amiss. Jia Zheng gave him a few instructions, and Baoyu assented to them. Jia Zheng had someone help him back, then went himself to Lady Wang’s room, where he earnestly charged her to discipline their son and never again indulge him as she had before. He insisted that Baoyu must sit the provincial examination the following year. Lady Wang listened to every word and mentioned nothing else. She hurriedly ordered attendants to support Baochai as they brought her in to perform the farewell rites of a new daughter-in-law; Baochai did not otherwise leave the room. The other women of the household all accompanied him as far as the second gate, then turned back. Jia Zhen and the others also received a stern admonition. Everyone raised a cup to see him off, and a company of younger clansmen, juniors, relatives, and friends escorted him all the way to the Long Pavilion ten li away, where they took their leave. We shall say no more of Jia Zheng setting out to take up his official post. Let us instead tell how, after Baoyu returned, his old illness suddenly flared up. He grew still more delirious and could no longer take even food or drink. Whether he lived or died remains unknown; the next chapter will reveal it.
